title: Post-Processing Workflow for Alaska Landscape Shots: Depth, Color, and Panoramas in Camera Raw/Photoshop

date.display: July 15, 2026 (approx. based on embedded export time)

locations.name: Alaska (probable shooting location)
locations.basis: Transcript repeatedly references an Alaska trip, Alaska landscapes, and Anchorage.

locations.name: Saudi Arabia (mentioned as comparative example)
locations.basis: Transcript mentions a Saudi Arabia shot as a reference point for depth and processing techniques.

summary: The video presents a dense, technique-forward workflow for transforming Alaska landscape imagery through non-destructive RAW processing, compositing, and panorama construction. It foregrounds guiding principles such as creating depth via controlled darkening and light paths, extracting shadow detail, and accentuating color (rainbow/blue hues) with Camera Raw, selective color, and tonal-based color adjustments. The instructor repeatedly emphasizes non-destructive workflows (unlimited history, history states, multiple saved versions), zone-based processing (flowers, glacier, mountains, sky), and precision masking with brushes. It also covers advanced warping and stitching tools (distort+scale, perspective/puppet warp, clone painting) for panoramas, and documents practical workflow decisions around focus stacking vs. bracketing, tripod stability, and drone panoramas using PTGUI and PanoVolo, all set against Alaska trip footage and visuals.

Preserving shadow detail while darkening for tonality (avoid clipping shadows)
Starting RAW workflow in Camera Raw/Photoshop (Camera Raw filter)
Unlimited history in Photoshop to capture every edit state
Rainbow accentuation: using whites adjustment to enhance color and brightness
Balancing glacier/sky blues via blues, warmth, and saturation adjustments
History brush: painting adjustments from one history state into another with layer masking
Hard-edge masking for unselectable edges using 90% hard brush and 100% opacity
Fade techniques to conceal obvious edits and blend edges
Repeating adjustments (30% opacity passes) to build up effects non-destructively
De-haze and selective edge control to push depth and atmosphere
Zones concept: separating flowers, glacier, mountains, and sky for targeted processing
Selective color vs HSL for precise color shifts (blue flowers example)
Color grading with tonal-based color adjustments and iterative balancing
Sky replacement/overlay approaches and keeping horizon/edges coherent
Cloning/sky replacement using clone stamp for sky alignment in panoramas
Perspective warp vs puppet warp: warping techniques for refined composites
Panorama stitching workflows: PTGUI vs Lightroom vs PanoVolo, rectilinear vs fisheye options
Focus stacking workflow: load into stack, auto-align, and blend; distinguishing from bracketing
Non-destructive saving strategy: saving multiple versions to preserve options

sections.title: Establishing depth and guiding the viewer's eye through light
concepts: big-to-small depth
drawing the eye along the light path
planning depth by darkening to create a guided visual path
sections.description: The speaker describes composing for depth by leveraging lighting differences (backlit peaks, brighter highlights) and a heavy-handed initial dark pass to establish a visual path from the light source into the mountains.

sections.title: Non-destructive history workflow
concepts: unlimited history in Photoshop
recording every brush stroke as a history state
painting adjustments by history state with the history brush
sections.description: The presenter demonstrates enabling unlimited history in Photoshop and explains using history states to non-destructively apply and revert edits, then painting those states back into a composite image.

sections.title: Camera Raw workflow and rainbow enhancement
concepts: Camera Raw filter in Photoshop
white's adjustment as a luminosity tool
balancing rainbow visibility via whites, blues, warmth, and global saturation
painting the adjustment into the image with history state masking
sections.description: Camera Raw is used to push global tonality, bring out the rainbow, and maintain color balance (glacier color) while preserving depth. The whites adjustment is demonstrated to recover contrast and saturation and is applied selectively using masking/history.

sections.title: Depth control with haze, dehaze, and edge refinement
concepts: de-haze for atmospheric depth
selective masking to apply haze to background layers
hard-edge brush for non-selectable mountains
edge refinement and feathering
sections.description: The instructor uses de-haze to push background depth, then applies targeted haze via masks and hard-edge brush techniques, followed by careful edge erasing and feathering to maintain realism.

sections.title: Layered adjustments and zone-based refinement
concepts: zones: flowers, glacier, mountains, sky
global vs local adjustments and fades
layered workflow and non-destructive stacking
starting with a dark pass and progressively lifting midtones
sections.description: A multi-zone approach is presented, with deliberate sequencing of adjustments per zone and fades to create coherent depth and mood across the image while preserving as much detail as possible.

sections.title: Sky and color grading with tonal-based adjustments
concepts: zone-based processing for sky and flowers
color grading using tonal-based color adjustments
color matching between sky and subject colors (blue/flower hues)
sections.description: The section covers sky color grading, tonal-based color adjustments, and iterative color matching to ensure harmony between sky, flowers, and glacier tones, with emphasis on preserving natural look while enhancing mood.

sections.title: Drone panorama workflow and stitching tools
concepts: PTGUI vs PanoVolo for drone panoramas
rectilinear vs other projections
auto exposure matching and sky/foreground balance
drone file organization and import considerations
sections.description: The presenter discusses the practicalities of drone panoramas, including stitch software choices (PTGUI generally preferred over Lightroom), the importance of exposure matching, and organizational tips for drone files to ensure clean stitching.

sections.title: Non-destructive saving and versioning strategy
concepts: saving multiple versions of the same composition
avoiding destructive editing by preserving unedited sources
using clone-paint and non-destructive blend methods to compare outcomes
sections.description: A closing emphasis on non-destructive workflows: saving multiple versions, avoiding destructive edits, and using clone-paint and layering to maintain options for future adjustments.
